notes:
A Wings of the Goddess quest that crosses eras, and the page is careless about saying which era each bullet is in. Two determinations were needed. (1) Leonhardt's zone is never written, in bullet 2 or bullet 5. The resolver says there is no Metalworks [S] at all -- only the present-day Metalworks (237) exists -- and the page instructs no travel between bullets 1 and 2, so Leonhardt is read as standing beside Ferghus in the Craftsmen's Eatery. (2) Bullet 3 says 'Bastok Markets (S)' and bullet 6 says plain 'Bastok Markets', and those are two different zones (87 and 235), both of which resolve. Taken literally that makes Raginmund a past NPC and Umberto his present counterpart at the same landmark -- Harmodio's Music Shop (L-10) -- which is an ordinary Wings of the Goddess shape and is what is recorded. If the missing (S) in bullet 6 is a typo instead, that one marker lands an era out, which is why the quest is medium.

Bullet 4 is a farm across two past zones, so it gets no zone rather than an arbitrary one; the Red Oven Mitt is the only observable thing in the quest and is not the reward (that is Aileen's Delight). Every other bullet is a genuine step -- there is no filler on this page.

notes:
Two top-level bullets and a real fork hidden in bullet 2's sub-bullets: if this is not your first Trust quest you are finished the moment you speak to Excenmille, and if it is, you must go cast the spell in Ronfaure and come back. Both branches are kept as one ladder, with the San d'Oria Trust permit carried on the LAST step rather than on step 2. That is a deliberate stretch of 'evidence must be obtained at that step' -- for a returning player it really is granted at step 2 -- but it is the only placement that reads correctly on both branches: holding the permit means the whole thing is over either way, whereas putting it on step 2 would leave a finished player with a live marker on Excenmille.

The header's Reward field lists BOTH key items, including the Red institute card that bullet 1 hands you at the very start. That is the wiki using Reward as 'everything you end up with', not as proof the quest is over, so the card is still used as step 1's evidence. Step 3 is the spell cast: no target, and West Ronfaure or East Ronfaure either one, so no zone. 'Level 5 on any job' is the level gate restated, so jobs stays empty.

notes:
Four bullets, two of which are not steps. Bullet 1 is a scarcity warning -- one player per Vana'diel day per world -- and bullet 4 is an outcome: completing it a second time grants the Lamp lighter's membership card, which is a reward and never evidence. The trailing line about Vhana Ehgaklywha lighting the lamps if nobody takes the quest is lore.

The twelve streetlamps are ONE step, not twelve. They are the same entity name in one zone, nothing reports how many are lit, and twelve identical rungs the player cannot be tracked through would be pure noise. The page writes the plural 'Streetlamps'; the entity is recorded singular, which is the only form that can match a live object. Both clocks -- the 18:03 to 21:00 window to accept and the 01:00 deadline to finish -- are game time and invisible to the addon. The turn-in is real: the sub-bullet says you can return to Zauko after 01:00 for credit.

The three items are a single AND-list handed over in one trade, and they are requirements to perform the step, not evidence that it is done -- nothing is observable after the trade because the reward is gil and a pair of armlets.

The farming sub-bullet names only monster FAMILIES -- ghosts, undead, hounds in The Eldieme Necropolis -- and never an actual monster, so no mob is recorded. Inventing one would be exactly the guessing this pass exists to avoid.

notes:
The eleven-way OR is the whole quest, and it models cleanly: eight of any ONE of eleven junk items. Beastcoin x8 is carried as the AND-list and the other ten sets as independent alternatives, all of which resolved, so items_partial stays false. The walkthrough only says 'eight (8) of any one of the items' -- the list itself is the header's Item Reqs, which is where the names come from.

Goblin Diggers are named in bullet 1 as the reason these things exist buried in the ground, not as something you fight, so no mob is recorded; the sub-bullet says Auction House, chocobo digging or unnamed monsters. Fame 'Other' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing, so region is null and only the raw is kept. No step carries evidence: holding eight of something is what you need to perform the trade, not proof you have done it.

notes:
A tidy little quest with two real evidence points: the empty Land of Milk and Honey hive at step 1 and the Full one at step 3, both genuine key items and neither of them the reward (that is Toxin resilience and 500 Bayld). Bullet 2 is the walk southwest to the swarm, not a step -- it is folded into the click that follows, since one step has one target and the target is the Pollinating Swarm either way.

The bee count is the unobservable part: you click the swarm, /heal until it says ten, then stand up, and nothing in that reports progress. The second click is a separate rung because it is a separate interaction that yields a different key item. The '(Optional)' return to Rumin-Flumin is the page's own word and is kept as an optional step; the reward comes from Ndah Tolohjin in Eastern Adoulin instead, which the page writes as 'Ndah Tolohjin (North)' -- that folds to the same key, so the plain form is recorded. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

The header puts 'Umbril Ooze' under Quest Reqs where it is plainly an item requirement, and Item Reqs is empty; the item is used as such and the misfiled field is flagged rather than turned into a prerequisite quest.

notes:
Nine bullets, every one of them an action, and the longest clean ladder in this batch. Two splits were needed. Bullet 8 -- 'Kill Badshah and re-examine the ??? to obtain Silver Comet's collar' -- is a fight and then an examine, so it becomes two rungs sharing the bullet number; the collar is a key item, not an inventory item, and it belongs to the examine that yields it, not to the kill. Bullet 4's three Warding Oils get their own obtain step in Beadeaux with the oils as evidence, because holding three of them is exactly the observable that says the farm is done and the gate is ready for them.

The Outpost Gate at the Pashhow Marshlands Outpost is examined at bullet 3 and traded to at bullet 5, with the farm in between, so those are two separate steps on the same object -- the page really does send you away and back. Same for the two Wobke visits. The sub-bullet warning that the cutscene implies a two-day deadline is explicitly contradicted by the page itself, so it is a note, not a time gate. Promathia Mission 3-2 sits in Quest Reqs rather than Previous; it is recorded as a prerequisite title anyway, since that is the only slot the schema has for it, and flagged. The expansion field is empty even though that mission is Chains of Promathia, so it is left null rather than derived.

notes:
Three bullets, but the quest does not end at bullet 3 -- the actual finish is buried in a sub-bullet ('Trade the Castle Floor Plans back to Dauperiat for your reward'), and the sub-bullet under that says in as many words that you have to turn the plans in for the quest to register as complete. So the farm and the hand-in are both steps taken from sub-bullets of bullet 3.

Halver has no zone anywhere on the page -- the description calls him Monarlais Halver, the walkthrough just Halver -- so the step carries no zone rather than an invented one. That costs nothing here: the name is not an ambiguous one, so the marker matches him wherever he is standing. Delivering the Suspicious envelope is recorded as a talk carrying the key item, not a trade, since the page says 'deliver' and nothing about trading. The refusal branch in bullet 3 ('if you chose no') does not change the ladder -- it just abandons it; it is worth knowing that The Setting Sun can be flagged on fame alone, so declining costs nothing but this quest's completion.

notes:
Samurai artifact quest, so 'Level: 40+ Samurai' is BOTH gates: level 40 and jobs ['SAM']. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false.

The one judgement call is the fight. The page never writes 'kill Isonade' -- bullet 3 pops him, a sub-bullet gives his ~6,100 HP, and bullet 4 tells you to re-examine the ???. A player reads that as a fight, and a ladder that skipped it would jump straight from the trade to the reward examine, so the kill is recorded as its own rung with the bullet numbers it came from. Bullet 4 is then the examine that yields the Handful of crystal scales, which is a key item and the second of the quest's two evidence points.

Bullet 2's travel is folded into the farm it exists to serve -- one obtain step in The Sanctuary of Zi'Tah, which the page happens to write with its article ('the The Sanctuary of Zi'Tah'), so no article was added. The page calls the traded item 'the Fish Bait'; the header's 'Sack of Fish Bait' is the same item and is the long form, so that is what is recorded. The description says the ritual needs both the mumeito and the crystal scales, but bullet 5 names only the Mumeito as the thing you trade -- the scales are the key item you are already carrying -- so only the Mumeito is a requirement of the last step.
